correctness.rationale: Bilinear expansion gives xy=r(x)c(y)^T. The margin map onto the common-total hyperplane W is surjective by filling the first row and column, and has kernel dimension d. Pair equations for a tuple with nonzero margins on both sides force at least one mixed row, then proportionality of all margin rows to it. Otherwise all first or all second margins are zero. Thus the reduced locus is exactly the rank-at-most-one cone in W^m and the two pure loci, times affine dm-space. For m≥2, either pure side is contained in the cone exactly when its margin space is one-dimensional; a mixed point prevents the reverse containment. The rank-one parametrization gives dimension a+b+m−2 before adding dm. All equations and noncontainment tests are valid also in characteristic two. Counting the two pure loci, subtracting their common zero, then counting q^m−1 tuples on each of the N/(q−1) mixed lines gives the exact bracketed formula. At m=0 it gives 1 and at m=1 it gives q^(ab). The recorded finite checks were inspected, not rerun; the proof does not depend on them.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: In a commuting tuple either a mixed coordinate exists, forcing the whole tuple onto its line, or all nonzero coordinates lie on the same pure side, since a nonzero pure next to the opposite nonzero pure cannot commute. Equivalently apply the biclique result to the span of the rows and intersect with W. Closing mixed-line tuples gives the rank-one cone on W; the pure loci have horizontal dimensions a−1 and b−1 and are contained in the cone iff that dimension is 1. This gives all components, dimensions, and thresholds. Counting lines with a mixed generator in W gives N/(q−1), and each contributes q^m−1 tuples; the two pure counts and free affine factor require only their known dimensions. No higher-arity analysis beyond these direct steps is needed.
